title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 124 (Contract of indemnity defined)

content.overview: Section 124 defines a contract of indemnity as a contract by which one party promises to save the other from loss caused to him by the conduct of the promisor himself, or by the conduct of any other person.
content.glance: Promise to save the promisee from loss caused by the promisor’s own conduct or by the conduct of any other person.
content.study: A contract of indemnity is a promise by one party (indemnifier) to save the other (indemnity-holder) from loss caused by the conduct of the promisor himself or by the conduct of any other person. The statutory illustration is: A contracts to indemnify B against the consequences of any proceedings which C may take against B in respect of a certain sum of 200 rupees; this is a contract of indemnity. Current-law framing: identify the promise to save from specified loss; identify the causative conduct (promisor or third person); apply the definition before considering rights under s. 125.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.body: A contract by which one party promises to save the other from loss caused to him by the conduct of the promisor himself, or by the conduct of any other person, is called a contract of indemnity.

sections.heading: Statutory illustration
sections.body: A contracts to indemnify B against the consequences of any proceedings which C may take against B in respect of a certain sum of 200 rupees. This is a contract of indemnity.

examples.title: Statutory illustration
examples.body: A contracts to indemnify B against the consequences of any proceedings which C may take against B in respect of a certain sum of 200 rupees. This is a contract of indemnity.

hypotheticals.question: Does a promise to reimburse losses caused by a third party’s act fall within section 124?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes, if it is a promise to save the promisee from loss caused by the conduct of any other person.

distinctions.title: Indemnity (s. 124) vs guarantee (s. 126)
distinctions.left: Promise to save from loss caused by promisor or another
distinctions.right: Contract to perform the promise or discharge the liability of a third person on default

misconceptions.trap: Indemnity covers only losses caused by the promisor.
misconceptions.correction: Section 124 expressly includes loss caused by the conduct of any other person.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 124 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the promise. II. Test whether it is a promise to save from loss caused by the promisor or any other person. III. Apply the definition and illustration. IV. Conclude.

revisionPoints: Caused by promisor or any other person
